body:
Found by the post-arc seam audit (T34 x T139), 2026-08-13. Mechanics confirmed in code; the
decision is Myk's because either resolution changes a stated promise.

WHAT IS TRUE. T139 made spawn and render two SEQUENTIAL hard windows in renderInWorker: a spawn
clock armed at construction, then `online` re-arms a FRESH render clock. The pool call site
(renderers.ts) deliberately refuses the host's 10s spawn ceiling -- that widening was caught and
reverted before #383 merged -- and passes the pool's own `renderTimeoutMs` as BOTH budgets.

THE RESIDUE. Both windows read the same number, and they run in sequence, so one render can hold
its envelope slot for up to 2x the declared clock. Declare 500ms; a loaded host spawns at 499ms;
the bundle then renders 499ms; the slot was held ~998ms. spec/24-quarantine.md says
`renderTimeoutMs` is "the pool's own wall clock, per render" and that "the envelope is the pool's
whole bill" -- and envelopeReports() prints the declared 500 with no field that can show the
doubling. The sentence is no longer exact. Severity is modest: the bound is real, proportional to
the operator's own knob, and 2x at worst -- nothing is unbounded.

THE OPTIONS, one must be chosen (Myk):
(a) SUM SEMANTICS, SAY SO. Amend §24.5 at the next landing: a pool render is bounded by spawn +
    render, each at the declared clock, worst case 2x. Cheapest; the report stays as it is; the
    promise becomes exact again by weakening one sentence.
(b) ONE BILL, ENFORCED. The pool path arms spawn with the declared clock and re-arms the render
    window with the REMAINDER (declared minus elapsed spawn). The sentence stays as strong as
    written; the cost is a new renderInWorker mode (the primary doors keep T139's two independent
    budgets -- that split is the whole point of T139 and must not regress).
(c) REPORT THE DOUBLING. Keep sum semantics but surface it: envelopeReports() carries a worst-case
    hold field. Weakest; the promise text still needs (a)'s amendment.

RAILS for whichever lands: the forwarding rail (test/gateway/render-spawn-forwarding.test.ts)
already pins WHICH numbers reach the pool site and must be extended to pin the chosen semantics;
option (b) additionally wants a wall-clock rail proving a slot is never held past the declared
clock plus scheduling slack.
title: A pool render can bill up to twice its declared clock — §24.5's "whole bill" sentence is no longer exact
